equation_request.abstract:
We present a quantum Viterbi algorithm (QVA) with better than classical performance under certain conditions. In this paper the proposed algorithm is applied to decoding classical convolutional codes, for instance; large constraint length $Q$ and short decode frames $N$. Other applications of the classical Viterbi algorithm where $Q$ is large (e.g. speech processing) could experience significant speedup with the QVA. The QVA exploits the fact that the decoding trellis is similar to the butterfly diagram of the fast Fourier transform, with its corresponding fast quantum algorithm. The tensor-product structure of the butterfly diagram corresponds to a quantum superposition that we show can be efficiently prepared. The quantum speedup is possible because the performance of the QVA depends on the fanout (number of possible transitions from any given state in the hidden Markov model) which is in general much less than $Q$. The QVA constructs a superposition of states which correspond to all legal paths through the decoding lattice, with phase a function of the probability of the path being taken given received data. A specialized amplitude amplification procedure is applied one or more times to recover a superposition where the most probable path has a high probability of being measured.

**Key words and phrases:**

Viterbi Algorithm and Hidden Markov Model and Convolutional Code and Tensor-Product Structure and Butterfly Diagram and Amplitude Amplification and Quantum Function Optimum Finding

specification.problem: Find the most probable legal path through a decoding trellis (hidden Markov model with fanout f much less than the number of states) given received data, by preparing a superposition over all legal paths with path-probability-dependent phase and applying amplitude amplification.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny assumed instance: a trellis with N=2 decode steps, binary fanout f=2, and 2^(Q-1) states with Q=3. The scope covers uniform path superposition over legal paths, a generic path-score phase, and a generic amplitude amplification iteration. The specialized amplitude amplification, the FFT-butterfly-based state preparation, the speedup analysis and the Quantum Function Optimum Finding details are outside scope.

equations.label: Legal path count
equations.description: Number of legal paths when each state has f outgoing transitions and S_0 start states are allowed.
equations.abstract_quote: the performance of the QVA depends on the fanout (number of possible transitions from any given state in the hidden Markov model)
equations.justification: Inferred from the fanout-dependence claim; the counting itself is elementary trellis combinatorics.

equations.label: Path superposition with phase
equations.description: Superposition of all legal paths with phase being a function of path probability given y.
equations.abstract_quote: constructs a superposition of states which correspond to all legal paths through the decoding lattice, with phase a function of the probability of the path being taken given received data
equations.justification: Direct reading of the claim; uniform amplitudes are assumed since the abstract does not state them.

equations.label: Phase as function of path probability
equations.description: Phase depends on the path posterior, factorized by the HMM structure; g is not specified.
equations.justification: Standard HMM factorization; the mapping g is a placeholder because the abstract gives no schedule.

equations.label: Grover-type amplification
equations.description: Generic amplitude amplification toward the marked most-probable path; the specialized procedure of the paper is not reproduced.
equations.justification: Textbook amplitude amplification, standing in for the paper's specialized procedure.
assumptions: Marking oracle for the best path assumed to exist

registers.name: path
registers.role: encodes the sequence of transition choices defining a legal path

registers.name: phase_ancilla
registers.role: workspace to compute path score and phase, uncomputed afterward

specification.initial_state: All-zero state on the path register, assumed.

steps.description: Prepare uniform superposition over legal paths, using a tensor product of per-step transition choices (assumed Hadamards for f=2).
Apply generic amplitude amplification iterations toward the most probable path.

specification.measurement: Measure the path register in the computational basis to read out the candidate most probable path.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map the measured transition choices to a state sequence and decoded bits; optionally verify the path score classically.
assumptions: Tiny instance Q=3, N=2, f=2 chosen by this reconstruction
Uniform amplitudes and generic Grover amplification used in place of the unspecified specialized procedure
Phase function g is a placeholder
